questions.question: In a certain code language, "SHOES – NAIL" is written as "30". How is "BRING – NAIL" written in that code language?
questions.solution:
The place value of ‘SHOES’ in English alphabet is = 19 + 8 + 15 + 5 + 19 = 66

And the place value of ‘Nail’ in English alphabet is = 14 + 10 + 12 = 36

So, "SHOES – NAIL" is written as = 66 – 36 = "30".

Therefore, the place value of ‘BRING’ in English alphabet is = 2 + 18 + 9 + 14 + 7 = 50.

Hence, "BRING – NAIL" is written as = 50 – 36 = 14.

questions.question: Raman's age is 37 years. If 10 years ago, Bhushan's age was one-third of Raman's age, then after how many years will Bhushan's age be 60 years?
questions.solution:
Raman's age is 37 years. 

So, 10 years ago, Raman’s age was 27 years.

Thus, 10 years ago, Bhushan’s age = 27 ÷ 3 = 9 years

Now, Bhushan’s age = 9 + 10 = 19 years

Therefore, Bhushan's age after 60 years will be: (60 – 19) = 41 years.

questions.question: A shopkeeper claims to sell his goods at cost price but uses a weight of 225 grams for a 250 grams weight. What is the profit percentage for the shopkeeper?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Profit Percentage** = (Error ÷ Weight Sold) × 100

Error = **True Weight** − **False Weight** = 250 g − 225 g = 25 g

Profit % = (25 ÷ 225) × 100

Profit % = (1 ÷ 9) × 100 = 11.11%

**∴ The correct answer is 11.11%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

True Weight = **250 g**

False Weight Used = **225 g**

Claimed Condition = Selling at **Cost Price (CP)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6614d8bddb8d20aa91d9bcfa3c11afc85eead8c9699e9dd5e11e947a8ad9f555.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 g of goods be ₹1.

⇒ The shopkeeper claims to sell 250 g at its **CP**, which is ₹250.

⇒ Therefore, the **Selling Price (SP)** of the quantity sold is ₹250.

⇒ However, he actually gives only **225 g** to the customer.

⇒ The **Actual CP** of the quantity sold (225 g) = 225 × 1 = ₹225.

⇒ **Profit** = SP − CP = 250 − 225 = ₹25.

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (25 ÷ 225) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 9) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 11.11%

**∴ The correct answer is 11.11%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

A dealer is dishonest if he uses a weight less than the true weight. The profit is always calculated on the **actual weight** delivered to the customer.

Successive Profit/Loss

If a dealer sells at a **markup of x%** and uses **y% less weight**, the overall profit % = [(100 + x) ÷ (100 − y) − 1] × 100.

Ratio Method for False Weight

The ratio of **CP to SP** can be expressed as: CP/SP = (False Weight) / (True Weight), provided the price per unit remains the same.

Sum of n terms of AP = n/2(2a + (n - 1)d) where ‘a’ is first term and ‘d’ is common difference

Let the first odd number be x

Sum of first 7 odd numbers = 7/2(2x + 6 × 2) = 7x + 42

Average of first 7 odd numbers = (7x + 42)/7 = x + 6 = A

New first term in new case = x - 6

Sum of 14 odd numbers = 14/2(2(x - 6) + 13 × 2) = 14(x + 7) = 14x + 98

Average of 14 odd numbers = (14x + 98)/14 = x + 7 = A + 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Contiguous**" refers to things that are touching or sharing a common border or boundary. Therefore, the opposite of "**contiguous**" would be something that is not touching or sharing a common border or boundary.
 
• "**Inaccessible**" is the word that fits this description, as it means **something that is not easily reached or approached.**
 
• Example sentence using "**contiguous**":
 
 
• *The two countries had **contiguous **borders and shared many cultural and economic ties.*
 
 
 
• Example sentence using "**inaccessible**":
 
 
• *The peak of the mountain was **inaccessible **due to the rough terrain and dangerous conditions.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** option 4) inaccessible.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's have a look at the **meaning **of other words in options:-

 
 
• "**Adjacent**" means next to or adjoining something else. It is a synonym of "contiguous" and, therefore, not an antonym.
 
• "**Abutting**" means bordering or adjoining something else. It is also a synonym of "contiguous" and, therefore, not an antonym.
 
• "**Bitterness**" means having a harsh and disagreeable taste, or a feeling of resentment or hostility. It is not related to the meaning of "contiguous" and, therefore, not an antonym.

• The error lies in **part 2 **of the sentence. 
 
• The word **than** is wrong here as it is contextually wrong.
 
• The word **when** should be used here as it gives proper meaning to the sentence. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7aa83af99ce472524089f105a39231d420512e90e6e735e1c21953d903076977.png] **Point to note**

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Her son has done and (1)/ is still doing excellent (2)/ work for his business. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically and contextually correct.
 
• In a compound sentence, both the **auxiliary verbs** and **main verbs **should be mentioned separately if they differ in number, form or voice.
 
• For example:
 
 
• Dexter has not and will not fail in the near future. (incorrect)
 
• Dexter has not **failed **and will not** fail** in the near future. (correct) (Here, the form of “fail” is different. One is “failed” and the other one is “fail”)
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this question, 'done' and 'doing' are two different forms of verb. Hence, they should be mentioned separately.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **4) No error**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• However, if the number, form and voice don’t differ, the auxiliary verb and main verb shouldn’t be mentioned separately.
 
 
• For example: I did not and will not go there. (correct) (Students might mistakably put “go” after “did not”. But the form, voice or number doesn’t differ. So, “go” will be omitted.)
